_note: Realistic multi-drug scenarios (FIX_PLAN Phase 5). The danger comes from different compositions prescribed together, often hidden inside a combination brand, not from one molecule under two names. Brands and compositions are from public/data/brands.json. Provenance tier T3 (docs/TEST_PLAN.md): the cases and the expected tiers are ours; 'review' stays null until a named reviewer judges the case. 'expect' lists alerts that must appear with that exact tier; 'interrupts' is the exact set of Interrupt types (empty = none allowed); 'forbid' lists alert types that must not appear; 'clean' means nothing above Silent. Rows marked question:true are judgement calls listed in eval/reviewer_list.md section H.

scenarios.title: Post-MI patient, knee pain from a different doctor
scenarios.realism: Dual antiplatelets plus a statin and beta-blocker after a heart attack; an orthopaedic surgeon later adds a combination painkiller.

prescriptions.text: Ecosprin-AV 75 OD x30d; Clopikind 75 OD x30d; Metolar 25 BD x30d; Cardace 5 OD x30d

scenarios.title: Same patient, a GP adds acidity cover
scenarios.realism: Omeprazole is the commonest PPI added for gastric protection.

prescriptions.text: Ecosprin-AV 75 OD x30d; Clopikind 75 OD x30d; Metolar 25 BD x30d; Cardace 5 OD x30d

scenarios.title: Triple whammy: blood pressure pill with a hidden diuretic, plus a painkiller
scenarios.realism: A chronic telmisartan-hydrochlorothiazide tablet and a short course of aceclofenac-paracetamol for joint pain.

scenarios.title: Warfarin, then co-trimoxazole for a urine infection
scenarios.realism: A patient with atrial fibrillation on warfarin gets a common UTI antibiotic from a GP.

scenarios.title: Warfarin, then metronidazole from a dentist
scenarios.realism: Metronidazole is routine after dental work.

scenarios.title: Weekly methotrexate with co-trimoxazole
scenarios.realism: Rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate; a GP treats a UTI with co-trimoxazole.

scenarios.title: Methotrexate written as a daily medicine
scenarios.realism: The classic fatal error: a weekly drug transcribed as OD.

scenarios.title: Gout colchicine with a hidden clarithromycin in an H. pylori kit
scenarios.realism: Pylokit is a common triple-therapy pack; the macrolide is not in its name.

scenarios.title: An older woman with three sedating medicines from three doctors
scenarios.realism: Anxiety, neuropathy and poor sleep treated separately; a benzodiazepine hides inside an antidepressant combination.

scenarios.title: Antidepressant with tramadol and a cough syrup
scenarios.realism: Two serotonergic drugs are hidden in a combination painkiller and a cough syrup.

scenarios.title: Four QT-prolonging medicines in a woman of 66
scenarios.realism: Hydroxychloroquine for arthritis, then azithromycin, domperidone and ondansetron for a chest infection and nausea.

prescriptions.text: Azithral 500 OD x3d; Domstal 10mg TDS x3d; Emeset 4 SOS x3d

scenarios.title: Theophylline combination with ciprofloxacin
scenarios.realism: A COPD patient on Deriphyllin gets ciprofloxacin for a UTI.

scenarios.title: Phenytoin with a single fluconazole dose
scenarios.realism: A one-off antifungal dose for vaginal thrush in a woman on long-term phenytoin.

scenarios.title: Lithium with ibuprofen hidden in Combiflam
scenarios.realism: A dentist prescribes a common ibuprofen-paracetamol tablet to a patient on lithium.

scenarios.title: Heart failure with weak kidneys: potassium-raising drugs stack
scenarios.realism: Spironolactone and an ARB for heart failure; a GP adds co-trimoxazole for a UTI.

prescriptions.text: Aldactone OD x90d; Telma 40 OD x90d

scenarios.title: Diabetic kidney disease: sitagliptin above the kidney dose
scenarios.realism: Metformin-glimepiride, sitagliptin and an ARB in a 71-year-old with creatinine 1.9.
scenarios.rx: Glycomet-GP 2 BD; Januvia 100mg OD; Telma 40 OD

scenarios.title: Tuberculosis treatment with warfarin and a sulfonylurea
scenarios.realism: Rifampicin is a strong enzyme inducer; the four-drug TB pack hides isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol.

prescriptions.text: Glycomet-GP 2 BD x90d; Warf 5 OD x90d

scenarios.title: Angina nitrate with an erectile dysfunction tablet
scenarios.realism: The man buys sildenafil himself; the nitrate is on his cardiology prescription.

scenarios.title: Digoxin with newly started amiodarone, weak kidneys
scenarios.realism: A rhythm-control drug is added to digoxin in an elderly man.

scenarios.title: A child's fever: Meftal-P is not paracetamol
scenarios.realism: A paediatrician and a GP each give a syrup; the 'P' in Meftal-P is not paracetamol.

scenarios.title: Two as-needed paracetamol products
scenarios.realism: A stomach-cramp tablet and a fever tablet, both bought as needed.

scenarios.title: Penicillin allergy and the amoxicillin hidden in Mox-CV
scenarios.realism: The brand name does not say 'amoxicillin'.

scenarios.title: Pregnancy with an old blood-pressure and cholesterol prescription
scenarios.realism: A refill of medicines started before the pregnancy.

scenarios.title: A second doctor replaces the PPI
scenarios.realism: A new doctor switches pantoprazole to rabeprazole-domperidone without writing 'stop'.

scenarios.title: Two antibiotic courses a few weeks apart, one with no course length
scenarios.realism: A 30-day default would invent an overlap; the ordered quantity (10 tablets, twice a day) says five days.

scenarios.title: A cart with products and no dosing
scenarios.realism: E-pharmacy carts hold products and pack counts, not a frequency.

scenarios.title: A lab eGFR with no weight or creatinine
scenarios.realism: The platform's lab reports eGFR; the pharmacy does not know the weight.
